note: Calling a speeder (the Ledger's Call button by each of your speeders). Read by src/systems/world/speeder_post.gd (SpeederPost.call_speeder). Home planet only: your speeders live there. It parks on open, flat sand near where you called from: from park_min_m out, ring by ring every park_step_m to park_max_m, a circle park_room_m round with nothing in it and no more than flat_m up or down, nearest first and on the side the speeder is on. It needs a straight run in skip_m long: walked out from the spot every run_step_m, the sand underfoot rising or falling no more than run_rise_m a step (no walls, roofs or mesa edges) and nothing within run_radius_m (lift_m: how high over the sand each step is dropped from); run_tries headings are tried per spot, from the speeder's side round. sample_budget caps the steps one call may walk, and search_ms is how much of a physics frame the search may take (the rest waits for the next frame, so a call never hitches; the speeder sets off once its spot is found). Further than skip_m from the spot (or with no clear run from where it is), the speeder skips to the far end of that run and drives itself in with nobody aboard (the 'valet' driver, content/core/vehicles/speeder_drivers.json); nearer, it drives from where it is. Inside the town's walls (its footprint, grown by town_margin_m) the streets are no place for a speeder: it pulls up by the town's own speeder spots outside instead (markers with a role in town_spots: the row by the back gate, the gate speeders'), the nearest to you first, within town_park_max_m of one, its run leaning away from town. Already within near_m of you: it stays put. On its spot and stopped, it is parked whichever way it faces. Still out after timeout_s (stuck behind something): it is set on its spot.

labels.call_nowhere: Nowhere open near here for a speeder to pull up.
